threads.body: [General] This comment describes a process-to-receive link that is not created. In stable mode the receive context is discarded here; both receive and process link extractors instead link to the producer creation context. Reword this to describe the actual parent behavior.

[General] RocketMQ can record `ConsumeReturnType.TIME_OUT` even when the listener eventually returns a success status, in which case `response.isSuccess()` is true. This early return therefore drops the documented `TIME_OUT` `error.type`; inspect `CONSUME_CONTEXT_TYPE` first and only use `isSuccess()`/status as the fallback classification.

replies.body: Addressed in 5d8a81082694a2308eacd0231c999852bf0d6658: Both error.type and the span status now derive from a shared getErrorType(ConsumeMessageContext) that inspects ConsumeReturnType first, so a listener that exceeds the consume timeout is reported as TIME_OUT even when its consume status is a success. Added unit tests for the timed-out and SUCCESS return types plus an end-to-end test asserting ERROR status with error.type=TIME_OUT, and clarified the README.

threads.body: [General] `isSuccess()` reflects the listener's returned consume status, not RocketMQ's `ConsumeReturnType`. A listener that returns success after the configured timeout has `ConsumeReturnType.TIME_OUT` but `isSuccess() == true`, so this leaves the span `UNSET` despite the newly documented timeout error. Include the consume-return type in the failure classification.
